latest_release.body:
﻿# Pinchflat-ngx 2026.11.2

This release adds bulk retries for failed downloads and fixes PostgreSQL downloads that fail when progress counters exceed 2 GiB. It also improves reliability for large SQLite-to-PostgreSQL transfers and provides clearer diagnostics during migration recovery.

Thanks to [@funar](https://github.com/funar) for highlighting the need for bulk permanent retries in [#200](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/discussions/200), [@Dav-Git](https://github.com/Dav-Git) for the detailed task-counter overflow report in [#201](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/issues/201), [@cbrookins](https://github.com/cbrookins) for reporting the migration validation failures, and [@joryirving](https://github.com/joryirving) for tracing large-file issues.

- **Bulk retry permanent failures and discarded jobs.** A dedicated **Force Retry Permanent** button is now available on **Media History > Failed** and individual source tabs to re-enqueue items after fixing root causes. In **Settings > Diagnostics > Failed Jobs**, **Reset All Discarded Jobs** allows retrying jobs that exhausted their maximum retry attempts. [Download recovery](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Download-recovery#retry-failed-downloads-in-bulk), [Diagnostics](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Diagnostics#queue-controls).
- **PostgreSQL 64-bit progress counters.** Downloaded bytes, total bytes, and download speed columns in PostgreSQL are widened to `bigint` (`int8`). Downloads larger than 2 GiB will no longer crash progress updates or exhaust their retries. ([#201](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/issues/201))
- **Large SQLite-to-PostgreSQL transfers.** Transfer validation reads batches by primary key ID instead of scanning offset windows, and normalizes timestamp precision across SQLite and PostgreSQL to avoid false checksum mismatches. [Migration guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/SQLite-to-PostgreSQL-migration#large-library-transfer-fixes).

Back up your database, configuration, and media before upgrading. Startup migrations will automatically widen task progress columns in PostgreSQL. Downloads that previously failed permanently due to the counter overflow can be re-queued with **Force Retry Permanent**. [Upgrade and rollback](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Upgrading-and-Rollback#upgrading-to-2026112).

## Container images

SQLite and PostgreSQL images are available at the versioned tags below and their moving aliases.

| Database   | Versioned image                                        | Moving tag        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| SQLite     | `ghcr.io/thebadfella/pinchflat-ngx:2026.11.2`          | `latest`          |
| PostgreSQL | `ghcr.io/thebadfella/pinchflat-ngx:2026.11.2-postgres` | `latest-postgres` |

Both database images include AMD64 and ARM64 manifests.

For pinned installations, update the image tag first. Pull and recreate the application service using your existing Compose setup, then check startup migrations, health, and Diagnostics. [Upgrading](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Upgrading-and-Rollback), [transfer guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/SQLite-to-PostgreSQL-migration).

Full changelog: [2026.11.1...2026.11.2](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/compare/2026.11.1...2026.11.2).

detail.readme:
An enhanced, self-hosted YouTube media manager built on Pinchflat.
Engineered with a Material 3 AMOLED interface, SQLite & PostgreSQL 18 support,
OIDC single sign-on, and local disk staging for seamless network storage downloads.

Overview • Comparison • Screenshots • Get Started • PostgreSQL • NAS Staging • OIDC SSO • Documentation

--- ## What Pinchflat-ngx adds ### Why Pinchflat-ngx? | Feature | Upstream Pinchflat | Pinchflat-ngx | | :----------------------- | :------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------- | | **Database** | SQLite only | SQLite & PostgreSQL 18 | | **User Interface** | Legacy theme | Material 3 AMOLED Dark Mode | | **Authentication** | HTTP Basic Auth only | Basic Auth + OAuth2 / OIDC (Authentik, Authelia, etc.) | | **Download Pipeline** | Direct write only | Local Disk Staging (NAS / NFS-friendly) | | **YouTube Reliability** | Stock yt-dlp | PO-token Provider (bgutil) integration | | **Queue Operations** | Basic worker pool | Live Diagnostics, Granular Worker Tuning | | **Single Video Sources** | No (Channel/Playlist only) | Yes (One-off direct video downloads) |

📚 Sources

More ways to add media, decide what downloads, and control where files land.

✨ Interface

A focused Material 3 AMOLED experience across desktop and mobile.

⬇️ Downloads

Better visibility, safer retries, and settings for real-world YouTube access.

🛠️ Operations

Queue controls, diagnostics, structured logs, and adjustable workers.

🔐 Access

Optional OAuth2/OpenID Connect login without breaking podcast clients.

📦 Delivery

Versioned, multi-platform container images published through GHCR.
### Sources - **Single video sources:** Add one-off YouTube video URLs directly instead of treating everything as a channel or playlist. - **Browse and URL intake:** Search YouTube, preview a video, paste a URL or subscribe to a channel from [Browse](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Browse-and-URL-intake). - **Batch source import:** Preview and import Google Takeout subscription CSVs or text URL lists with one media profile. [Import subscriptions](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Import-subscriptions). - **Bulk source management:** Pause or resume downloads, assign profiles and preview publication-date cutoff changes across selected sources. [Bulk actions](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Bulk-source-management). - **Import existing downloads:** Register media already on disk without downloading it again. [Import guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Import-existing-downloads). - **Bookmarklets and scoped share tokens:** Send a video from a browser or external shortcut using a chosen media profile. [Sharing guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Sharing-and-bookmarklets). - **Selective playlist downloads:** Index a playlist, review its items, and choose exactly what to fetch from the Selection flow. - **Stronger source controls:** See automatic and delayed sources at a glance, with inline and menu actions to start, pause, or stop them. - **Faster source actions:** Jump to a source from notifications and delete sources directly from their management views. - **Per-source folder routing:** Send each source to its own folder with a picker for existing directories and template-aware output paths. ### Interface - **Material 3 AMOLED theme:** Dark, consistent surfaces with shared semantic colors, spacing, controls, and hierarchy. - **Native Tailwind v4 pipeline:** Theme tokens and the native Tailwind v4 asset pipeline keep the interface consistent and maintainable. - **Cleaner forms:** Refined toggles, custom selects, clearer editing states, and better guidance when creating sources and profiles. - **Collapsible sidebar:** Collapse desktop navigation when you want a denser workspace. - **Mobile polish:** Source, job, history, profile, and settings views adapt cleanly to smaller screens. - **Settings search:** Filter Settings to find notifications, extractor options, cookies, and yt-dlp controls quickly. - **Latest across sources:** Filter recently indexed videos by date and group them by source. [Latest guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Latest-across-sources). - **Channel Discovery:** Review related channels found from local metadata and subscriptions; scanning is opt-in. [Discovery guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Channel-Discovery). - **Interface gallery:** Explore the [Screenshots](#screenshots) gallery below for full captures of the interface. ### Downloads - **Cookie management:** Upload, paste, and inspect the shared `cookies.txt` file from Settings. - **YouTube API-key testing:** Validate a key before relying on it for indexing. - **Unavailable-media handling:** Skip and label members-only, private, or removed videos instead of retrying forever. - **Clear media states:** The Other tab distinguishes Unavailable, Removed, Ignored, and Filtered Out items. - **Live speed visibility:** See current download speed in the jobs dashboard and media tables. - **Safer retries:** Retry flows clear stale errors and keep job and media state aligned. - **Controlled yt-dlp updates:** Choose stable, nightly, frozen nightly, nightly-until-stable, or a pinned version. - **yt-dlp base configuration:** Maintain additional yt-dlp options in Settings using familiar config-file syntax. - **Failed-download workflow:** Review failed items on Home and retry one or many from history and source tables. - **Cookie-aware forced retries:** Forced retries continue to apply cookies when livestream prechecks are skipped. - **Separate Shorts paths:** Choose a different output template for Shorts on a media profile. [Download settings](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Download-settings). ### Operations - **Queue diagnostics:** Inspect running, retryable, and discarded Oban jobs; reset or cancel individual jobs; and clear discarded queues. - **Worker concurrency:** Set separate limits for downloads, indexing, and metadata in Settings. Environment variables can override those saved values. - **Release status:** See whether Pinchflat-ngx is current and which yt-dlp update policy is active. - **Operational diagnostics:** Use structured source, indexing, enqueue, and skipped-download logs alongside responsive integrity and maintenance tools. - **Media-server refresh:** Notify Plex, Jellyfin or Emby after completed downloads. [Refresh guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Media-server-refresh). - **Database backups and transfer:** Create PostgreSQL dumps and review an in-app SQLite-to-PostgreSQL transfer. [Backups](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Backups-and-Restore), [transfer guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/SQLite-to-PostgreSQL-migration). - **Repository-friendly Compose layout:** Development Compose files live in `docker/`, while the root `compose.yaml` keeps `docker compose up` working for contributors. - **Current FFmpeg builds:** Images install FFmpeg from [yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds) `latest`. - **Ongoing fork improvements:** Smaller workflow, interface, and reliability changes continue to land as they prove useful in daily self-hosted use. ### New in 2026.11.0 Release **2026.11.0** adds the workflows below. See the [release notes](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/releases/tag/2026.11.0) for upgrade guidance and contributor thanks. - **Watch windows and saved originals:** Opt in to duration/visibility checks after new downloads, receive confirmed-change notifications and preserve originals before protected replacements. Checks do not detect every content edit. [Watch guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Watch-downloaded-videos). - **Profile retention defaults:** Leave a source's retention blank to inherit its profile, set a positive override or use `0` to disable age-based expiry. Effective-value previews show which rule applies. Changes can affect existing files. [Retention guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Retention-and-protection). - **Library views:** Find one-off sources in **Individual videos** and browse each source's **Videos** tab in list or grid view. [Individual videos](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Browse-and-URL-intake#find-individually-added-videos), [source views](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Source-settings#source-library-views). - **Download and indexing recovery:** Preserve uploaded cookies, retry authenticated thumbnails with **When Needed**, stop repeated retries for confirmed filter skips and report incomplete indexing runs. [Download recovery](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Download-recovery), [indexing health](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Indexing-health). - **Source URL support:** Accept YouTube Music/mobile URLs and inspect empty Watch Later playlists when YouTube returns collection metadata. Valid cookies and provider access requirements still apply. [Source setup](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Source-settings#source-type). - **Operations:** Record PostgreSQL files above 2 GiB, keep byte totals usable, open PostgreSQL backups from **Config > Backups**, and use Discord embed formatting for notifications. [Large-file migration](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/SQLite-to-PostgreSQL-migration#files-larger-than-2-gib), [backups](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Backups-and-Restore), [notifications](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Notifications). - **yt-dlp plugins:** Install trusted archives or use allowlisted direct URLs, edit per-plugin configuration, and update or remove packages in Settings. [Plugin setup and recovery](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/yt-dlp-plugins). ### Single sign-on Pinchflat-ngx can protect the web interface with OAuth2/OpenID Connect. It supports provider discovery, PKCE, state and nonce validation, configurable scopes, and fixed callback URLs for reverse-proxy deployments. OIDC replaces Basic Auth for browser routes when enabled. Feed endpoints retain Basic Auth and route-token support for podcast clients. General API endpoints require `BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` and `BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` when Basic Auth or OIDC is enabled. API clients send these credentials using HTTP Basic Auth; an OIDC browser session does not authorize API calls. With OIDC alone and no Basic Auth credentials, general API requests are rejected. Unconfigured trusted-network installations retain unauthenticated access. `/healthcheck` and `/api/spec` remain public; share intake uses its own scoped tokens. **[Set up OIDC →](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/OIDC-Single-Sign-On)** --- ## Screenshots Explore captures of the Material 3 AMOLED interface across key views: | [Poster Grid](docs/assets/screenshots/sources-grid.png) | [Source Details](docs/assets/screenshots/source-details.png) | | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | | [![Sources Poster Grid](docs/assets/screenshots/sources-grid.png)](docs/assets/screenshots/sources-grid.png) | [![Source Details](docs/assets/screenshots/source-details.png)](docs/assets/screenshots/source-details.png) | | [Sources Table](docs/assets/screenshots/sources-table.png) | [System Diagnostics](docs/assets/screenshots/diagnostics.png) | | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | | [![Sources Table](docs/assets/screenshots/sources-table.png)](docs/assets/screenshots/sources-table.png) | [![System Diagnostics](docs/assets/screenshots/diagnostics.png)](docs/assets/screenshots/diagnostics.png) | | [Dashboard & History](docs/assets/screenshots/dashboard.png) | [Channel Discovery](docs/assets/screenshots/channel-discovery.png) | | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | | [![Dashboard](docs/assets/screenshots/dashboard.png)](docs/assets/screenshots/dashboard.png) | [![Channel Discovery](docs/assets/screenshots/channel-discovery.png)](docs/assets/screenshots/channel-discovery.png) | --- ## Get started | 1 · Deploy | 2 · Configure | 3 · Build your library | | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Run the multi-platform image from GHCR. | Set your timezone and choose Basic Auth or OIDC. | Create a media profile, then add a channel, playlist, or video. | | **[Installation guide →](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Installation)** | **[Configuration →](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Environment-Variables)** | **[Pinchflat concepts →](https://github.com/kieraneglin/pinchflat/wiki)** | ```yaml services: pinchflat-ngx: image: ghcr.io/thebadfella/pinchflat-ngx:latest environment: TZ: America/Regina ports: - '8945:8945' volumes: - ./config:/config - ./downloads:/downloads restart: unless-stopped ``` Save this as `compose.yaml`, replace the timezone if needed, and run `docker compose up -d`. Open when the container is healthy. > [!TIP] > Migrating an existing library from upstream Pinchflat? See [Migrating from Pinchflat](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Migrating-from-Pinchflat) on the wiki. > for pre-migration backups, drop-in Compose configuration, and the migration review walkthrough. ### Retention schedule Set **Default retention period (days)** on a media profile to apply age-based cleanup to sources whose **Retention Period (days)** is blank. Set a positive period on a source to override the profile, or `0` to disable age-based cleanup for that source. Without either period, age-based cleanup is disabled. Files become eligible that many days after download and are removed on the next retention run. Changing a profile or a source's profile can make previously downloaded files eligible at the next run. Protected media is not deleted; a source's publication-date cutoff can still delete unprotected files sooner. `RETENTION_CRON` controls how often the retention worker runs. It defaults to `0 1 * * *` (daily at 01:00). `RETENTION_TIMEZONE` sets its timezone and defaults to `Etc/UTC`, independently of `TZ`. For example, to check every four hours in Berlin time: ```yaml environment: TZ: Europe/Berlin RETENTION_CRON: '0 */4 * * *' RETENTION_TIMEZONE: Europe/Berlin ``` Recreate the container after changing these variables. No custom startup command or `sed` patch is needed. Invalid or empty cron expressions and timezones cause startup to fail. Without these settings, retention continues to run daily at 01:00 UTC, even when `TZ` is configured. An explicit `RETENTION_TIMEZONE` follows daylight saving time where applicable. Other scheduled jobs retain their existing UTC schedules, so retention may run after quality upgrades or database maintenance when you change its schedule or timezone. Automatic quality upgrades skip media already eligible for retention deletion, including media that expires while its upgrade is queued. This prevents an upgrade from restarting an already expired retention period before cleanup runs. Media protected from deletion remains eligible for upgrades, and forced downloads retain their override. Successful downloads that are allowed still update the download timestamp as before. ### PostgreSQL image The `latest` image continues to use SQLite. To start a new installation with PostgreSQL, use the `latest-postgres` image and set `DATABASE_URL`: ```yaml services: pinchflat-ngx: image: ghcr.io/thebadfella/pinchflat-ngx:latest-postgres environment: DATABASE_ADAPTER: postgres DATABASE_URL: ecto://pinchflat-ngx:change-me@postgres/pinchflat-ngx TZ: America/Regina depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy ports: - '8945:8945' volumes: - ./config:/config - ./downloads:/downloads restart: unless-stopped postgres: image: postgres:18-alpine environment: POSTGRES_DB: pinchflat-ngx POSTGRES_PASSWORD: change-me POSTGRES_USER: pinchflat-ngx healthcheck: test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U pinchflat-ngx -d pinchflat-ngx'] interval: 5s timeout: 5s retries: 10 volumes: - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql restart: unless-stopped volumes: postgres-data: ``` The PostgreSQL image creates and migrates its own schema, but it does not copy data from an existing SQLite database. This PostgreSQL 18 example is intended for a fresh installation. PostgreSQL 16 or earlier volumes are not compatible with the PostgreSQL 18 server as-is; use an explicit PostgreSQL upgrade or `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` procedure before reusing existing PostgreSQL data. Keep using `latest` for an existing SQLite installation until you have migrated its data separately. > [!TIP] > The PostgreSQL image supports in-app `pg_dump` backups and retention policies. In **2026.11.0**, open **Config > Backups**. Older 2026.10.20 installations use **Settings > PostgreSQL Backups**. See the [Backups and restore guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Backups-and-Restore) for backup operations and restore commands. ### Optional PO-token provider The default compose above keeps the provider disabled. If YouTube presents SABR or authentication problems, add the following service and environment variable to your compose file: ```yaml services: pinchflat-ngx: environment: TZ: America/Regina POT_PROVIDER_URL: http://pot-provider:4416 pot-provider: image: brainicism/bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider:2.0.0 profiles: [pot-provider] restart: unless-stopped # No ports mapping: the unauthenticated provider stays on the Compose network. ``` Start the opt-in service with `docker compose --profile pot-provider up -d`. Pinchflat-ngx images include the matching bgutil yt-dlp plugin, and Diagnostics reports the provider's bounded `/ping` health check. Installing bgutil again through **Settings > yt-dlp > Plugins** is blocked; use `POT_PROVIDER_URL` instead. See the [official bgutil provider documentation](https://github.com/Brainicism/bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider) and [yt-dlp's PO-token guide](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide) for background and limitations. ### Optional yt-dlp plugins Pinchflat-ngx loads yt-dlp extractor and postprocessor plugins from `/config/extras/yt-dlp-plugins`. Install them from **Settings > yt-dlp > Plugins** by uploading a `.zip`, `.whl`, or `.egg`, or by pasting a direct archive URL. You can also place packages in that directory yourself because it lives on the persistent `/config` volume. A package is either a folder containing `yt_dlp_plugins/` (for example `my-plugin/yt_dlp_plugins/extractor/my_extractor.py`) or an archive whose root contains `yt_dlp_plugins/`. URL-installed plugins record their source URL so **Update** can re-fetch them on demand. Pinchflat-ngx does not update plugins in the background. Plugins bundled with Pinchflat-ngx, currently the bgutil PO-token plugin, cannot be installed again through this page. URL installs are limited to public HTTP(S) hosts. The built-in allowlist covers GitHub release assets. Add another host with `YT_DLP_PLUGIN_URL_ALLOWLIST=plugins.example.com,cdn.example.com`. Private or LAN mirrors also require `YT_DLP_PLUGIN_URL_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` and an explicitly allowlisted host. `YT_DLP_PLUGIN_URL_ALLOW_PRIVATE` accepts `true`, `1`, `yes`, or `on`; any other value leaves private addresses blocked. Each installed plugin has a **Config** button. The editor stores a yt-dlp config file for that plugin, and Pinchflat-ngx loads it with `--config-locations` through its main yt-dlp command runner. The modal shows the package's bundled README when present. Archive READMEs over 20 KB are not shown, and folder READMEs are cut off at 20 KB. The options file starts empty because yt-dlp plugins do not expose a config schema; use it for plugin-documented options such as `--use-postprocessor` or `--extractor-args`. Options apply globally, so keep them compatible with your other plugins. A zip-only install does not install Python dependencies; plugins that import packages such as `requests`, `pyotp`, or `nodriver` need those packages added to the container first. yt-dlp catches plugin import errors and continues, so Pinchflat-ngx scans command output for them. Failures are logged with a `[yt-dlp plugins]` prefix and sent to the configured Apprise server, deduplicated for one hour. > [!WARNING] > Plugins run arbitrary Python inside the container and can read files and environment variables > available to the app. Install only plugins you trust. If the Settings UI is reachable by > untrusted users, configure Basic Auth or SSO before installing plugins. Extractor plugins take > priority over built-in extractors, so a plugin can change or break downloads and indexing. > yt-dlp's plugin API is unstable and may break across yt-dlp updates. Managed plugins are loaded for indexing, metadata and downloads through the main command runner. Browse search uses a separate command and does not load these plugins or their configs. Postprocessor plugins still need `--use-postprocessor NAME` in the per-plugin config or base yt-dlp config. Existing bind mounts at `/etc/yt-dlp/plugins` continue to work. ### Optional local download staging Set `DOWNLOAD_STAGING_PATH` to an absolute path inside the container when downloads should complete on a local disk before their finished artifacts are transferred to `/downloads`. The default is disabled, so existing deployments keep their current direct-to-library behavior. Each download receives its own directory, and the database is updated only after the complete artifact set reaches the media root. For a local staging disk, add a bind mount such as: ```yaml services: pinchflat-ngx: environment: DOWNLOAD_STAGING_PATH: /staging volumes: - ./download-staging:/staging ``` For a NAS library with local temporary storage, mount the local staging disk separately from the NAS destination: ```yaml services: pinchflat-ngx: environment: DOWNLOAD_STAGING_PATH: /staging volumes: - /fast-local-disk/pinchflat-ngx-staging:/staging - /mnt/nas/media:/downloads ``` Staging and the media directory may be on different filesystems. Pinchflat-ngx uses a temporary destination name and an atomic rename after copying in that case. Staging paths must be absolute, writable, and different from the media root. --- ## Documentation | Start here | Run it safely | Understand the fork | | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Installation](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Installation) | [Backups and restore](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Backups-and-Restore) | [Pinchflat-ngx features](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Pinchflat-ngx-Features) | | [Migrating from Pinchflat](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Migrating-from-Pinchflat) | [Upgrading and rollback](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Upgrading-and-Rollback) | [Upstream Pinchflat wiki](https://github.com/kieraneglin/pinchflat/wiki) | | [Environment variables](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Environment-Variables) | [Diagnostics](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/Diagnostics) | API documentation at `/api/docs` on your instance | | [OIDC single sign-on](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/wiki/OIDC-Single-Sign-On) | [Backing up config before migration](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Backing-up-config-before-migration) | [SQLite to PostgreSQL migration](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/SQLite-to-PostgreSQL-migration) | The [Pinchflat-ngx wiki](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki) is the single source of truth for operator documentation. Shared concepts such as naming templates, media profiles, podcast feeds, SponsorBlock, retention, and custom scripts remain documented by upstream. --- ## Support and development - [Report a bug](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) - [Request a feature](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/issues/new?template=enhancement_request.yml) - [Browse releases](https://github.com/TheBadFella/pinchflat-ngx/releases) - [Roadmap](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Roadmap) for tracked enhancements not yet scheduled - Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for development commands and repository conventions Pinchflat-ngx is distributed under the terms in [LICENSE](LICENSE). For the optional SQLite transfer flow, see [SQLite to PostgreSQL migration](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/SQLite-to-PostgreSQL-migration) on the wiki.
